North China Daily News
December 29, 1934.

OBITUARY

Mrs. R. Audouard

The untimely death of Mrs. R.
Audouard occurred yesterday in the
Country Hospital at 2.40 p.m., as a
result of an overdose of a veronal
compound, taken as a sleeping potion.
According to report, the patient was
progressing favourably earlier yester-
day, with the attending physicians
being concerned only as to the
healthy condition of the heart.

Mrs. Audouard is survived by her
husband, Rolf Audouard, her father
and mother (Mr. and Mrs. J. Griffin),
who reside in Susanville, California,
a sister and a brother, the latter
having been a prominent athlete at
the University of California. A
younger brother is now studying at
the university.

Mrs. Audouard arrived in Shanghai
in the autumn of 1929, preceded by
a brilliant career in university circles
of journalism. Her connections with
local English language dailies, as well
as her signed articles to American
magazines, established her journalistic
career in Shanghai. On various
papers, her feature articles brought
her considerable popularity. Rec-
ognized papers, such as the "Chris-
tian Science Monitor", published her
contributions under her name. Dur-
ing the 1932 Sino-Japanese hostilities,
Mrs. Audouard contributed to local
publications and subsequently held
the editorship of "Health," at the
same time co-editing the "China
Digest."

After her freshman year at the
University of Nevada, Mrs. Audouard
completed her full course at the
University of California in less than
the prescribed time, graduating in
1928. Her career at the university
was amplified by extra-curricular
activities, which included running-up
for the place of "poetess-laureate"
on the campus. Under the advice
of Mr. Irving Pichel, professor of
dramatics and now a Hollywood star,
her diction and vivid expressiveness
brought her prominence in poetic
magazines as well as the humorous
monthlies.

Mrs. Audouard was married in
Shanghai during the summer of 1932,
and only returned to Shanghai after
long leave with her husband about
four weeks ago.

Funeral arrangements are in the
hands of the International Funeral
Directors, who are awaiting a reply
to a cabled notice to the deceased's
parents in Susanville, California.

《字林西报》
1934年12月29日。

讣告

R. 奥杜阿尔夫人

R. 奥杜阿尔夫人于昨日下午2时40分在乡村医院（Country Hospital）因服用过量作为安眠药的维罗那（veronal）复合制剂而英年早逝。据报告，病人昨日早些时候病情曾有好转，主治医生当时仅关注其心脏健康状况。

奥杜阿尔夫人身后留有丈夫罗尔夫·奥杜阿尔（Rolf Audouard）、父母（J. 格里芬夫妇，居住于加利福尼亚州苏珊维尔）、一位姐妹和一位兄弟，后者曾是加州大学的著名运动员。另一位弟弟目前正在该大学就读。

奥杜阿尔夫人于1929年秋季抵达上海，此前她在大学新闻界拥有辉煌的职业生涯。她与本地英文日报的联系，以及为美国杂志撰写的署名文章，奠定了她在上海的新闻事业基础。在各家报纸上，她的特写文章为她赢得了相当高的人气。《基督教科学箴言报》（Christian Science Monitor）等知名报刊均以署名形式刊登了她的稿件。在1932年中日冲突期间，奥杜阿尔夫人为本地出版物撰稿，随后担任《健康》（Health）杂志编辑，同时兼任《中国文摘》（China Digest）的联合编辑。

在内华达大学读完大一后，奥杜阿尔夫人以少于规定的时间完成了在加州大学的全部课程，并于1928年毕业。她在大学期间的经历因课外活动而更加丰富，其中包括竞选校园“桂冠女诗人”头衔。在戏剧学教授、现为好莱坞明星的欧文·皮切尔（Irving Pichel）先生的建议下，她的措辞和生动的表现力使她在诗歌杂志以及幽默月刊中崭露头角。

奥杜阿尔夫人于1932年夏季在上海结婚，并在与丈夫长期休假后，约四周前才返回上海。

丧事安排由国际殡仪馆（International Funeral Directors）负责，该馆正等待向死者位于加利福尼亚州苏珊维尔的父母发出的电报通知的回复。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, DECEMBER 28, 1934

FOREIGN WOMAN IS
FOUND POISONED

Mrs. R. Audouard Lying
In Critical State
At Hospital

RESCUERS FORCED TO
BURST OPEN DOOR

Some two hours after Reginald
Pickford was found dead in a hotel
room, police from Bubbling Well
Station attended another emergen-
cy call to discover Mrs. Merriam
Audouard of House No. 12, Lane
20, Seymour Road, lying in a semi-
conscious condition on the floor of
her home suffering from the effects
of veronal poisoning. She was
conveyed to the Country Hospital,
where everything possible was
done to save her life, but at a late
hour last night, doctors held out
little or no hope for her recovery.

First intimation of the affair
came when inmates of the house
heard groans and gasps issuing
from the apartment which she oc-
cupies with her husband, Mr. R.
Audouard, of Markt and Com-
pany. Efforts to open the door
proved fruitless, as it was locked
from the inside, and the police
were summoned to the scene.
Bursting into the room, they found
the woman in great agony and,
knowing that every moment was
precious if her life were to be
saved, rushed her to the hospital in
a station car, where she was treat-
ed by Dr. W. Nance.

Mrs. Audouard, who is 25 years
of age, was born in the United
States of America and is well-
known in Shanghai newspaper cir-
cles, having worked at various
times upon the different English
language dailies. At that time,
she was known as Miss Merriam
Griffin. A few years ago, she
married Mr. Audouard, a well-
known German business man.

The moment the police learnt of
the case, they notified the U.S.
District Attorney, Mr. Feltham
Watson, who is watching the case
on behalf of the United States
Government. Interviewed last
evening, Mr. Watson stated that
her marriage might have caused
her to forfeit her American citizen-
ship, but he strongly doubted it.
"I cannot make any definite state-
ment at the present time," he
added.

J.S.S.
JtR 29/2

《上海泰晤士报》，1934年12月28日，星期五

外籍女子被发现中毒

R. 奥杜阿尔夫人
在医院情况危急

救援人员被迫破门而入

在雷金纳德·皮克福德（Reginald Pickford）被发现死于酒店房间约两小时后，静安寺捕房的警员响应另一起紧急呼叫，发现居住在西摩路20弄12号的梅里亚姆·奥杜阿尔（Merriam Audouard）夫人躺在自家地板上，处于半昏迷状态，遭受维罗那中毒的影响。她被送往乡村医院，院方竭尽所能抢救其生命，但直到昨晚深夜，医生对她的康复已不抱希望或希望渺茫。

此事的最初迹象是，屋内住户听到她与其丈夫、马尔特公司（Markt and Company）的R. 奥杜阿尔先生共同居住的公寓里传出呻吟声和喘息声。试图打开房门的努力未果，因为门从内部锁住，警方遂被召至现场。警察冲进房间后，发现该女子极度痛苦，深知若要挽救其生命则分秒必争，遂用警车将其急送医院，由W. 南斯（W. Nance）医生进行救治。

奥杜阿尔夫人现年25岁，生于美利坚合众国，在上海新闻界颇有名气，曾先后在不同英文日报工作。当时她名为梅里亚姆·格里芬小姐（Miss Merriam Griffin）。几年前，她嫁给了德国著名商人奥杜阿尔先生。

警方获悉此案后，立即通知了美国地区检察官费尔瑟姆·沃森（Feltham Watson）先生，他正代表美国政府监视此案。沃森先生昨晚在接受采访时表示，她的婚姻可能导致其丧失美国公民身份，但他对此深表怀疑。“我目前无法做出任何确切的声明，”他补充道。

J.S.S.
JtR 12月29日/2
